description: Five canonical confidence levels applied to calculators, datasets, formulas, and reference pages to communicate the strength of the underlying evidence.

levels.label: Very High Confidence
levels.meaning: Value or calculation is derived from peer-reviewed scientific literature or formally adopted consensus standards (e.g., CDC, WHO, PHTA/ANSI, FINA). Multiple independent sources agree.
levels.typicalUse: Core chemistry constants, established safety limits, widely-adopted industry standards.
examples: Minimum ORP for disinfection (650 mV — WHO)

levels.label: High Confidence
levels.meaning: Value derived from well-established industry practice, widely adopted by professional pool operators, or supported by multiple manufacturer specifications with strong practitioner consensus.
levels.typicalUse: Recommended parameter ranges, standard dosage coefficients, common maintenance intervals.

levels.label: Moderate Confidence
levels.meaning: Value based on common practice supported by limited peer-reviewed evidence, or derived from industry guidance that has not been universally standardized. Some variation between sources.
levels.typicalUse: CYA/FC ratio guidance, phosphate thresholds, pool-specific recommendations that vary by surface type.
examples: CYA target range for saltwater pools
Pool-specific CH targets by surface material

levels.label: Limited Confidence
levels.meaning: Value derived from sparse sources, editorial interpretation, or emerging guidance not yet widely adopted. May vary significantly between manufacturers, regions, or pool conditions.
levels.typicalUse: Manufacturer-specific settings, regional regulatory variations, anecdotal industry practice.

levels.label: Informational
levels.meaning: Provided for general orientation only. Not a specific recommendation. Users should consult their product label, local health authority, or certified pool professional for their specific situation.
levels.typicalUse: General background information, illustrative examples, preliminary guidance pending further review.
examples: Background on why a chemical matters
Overview comparisons not intended for direct use
